## Summary
A one-tweet distillation of a 2026 SSRN paper, plus the author's own adaptation of its idea.

- **Paper:** SSRN 7268289, *Unexpected Gross Profit and Cross-Sectional Stock Returns* (2026). Core claim: firms reporting **higher-than-expected gross profit** — measured against their own **trailing 8 quarters** — tend to **outperform** cross-sectionally.
- **Author's assessment of the paper:** the in-paper results were **"tepid."**
- **His move:** took the concept (gross-profit surprise vs own trailing baseline) and **applied it to a microcap model**. The link to the public model is in the attached image, not the tweet body.

## Why it matters
- **New concept for the vault: fundamental surprise as a factor.** Not the classic earnings surprise (PEAD-adjacent) but **gross-profit surprise vs the firm's own trailing-8Q baseline** — a margins-focused, accrual-resistant measure of operational improvement. First fundamental-surface factor captured here; everything so far is technical/rules-based or prediction-market.
- **The microcap adaptation is the interesting part.** "Paper result tepid → sharpen it in microcaps" is a standard anomaly-hunting template: less analyst coverage, slower price discovery, wider dispersion — but also the regime where backtests lie hardest (see skepticism gates).
- **Evidence tier:** author-adapted model with **zero performance metrics quoted** in the tweet. At best self-backtest tier on the vault's evidence hierarchy; a public model + code (if the image delivers) is what makes independent replication possible — the standard set by [[2026-08-29-milk-man-replication-metrics]].
- **Skepticism gates:** paper results self-described as tepid; microcap backtests are structurally exposed to **liquidity/transaction costs, survivorship and delisting bias**; no Sharpe/drawdown/sample window given; the model link is unverified (locked in the attached image — unreadable in this capture pipeline); SSRN working paper ≠ peer-reviewed.
- **Isolation note (CoS convention):** personal second-brain knowledge capture only; nothing routed to the trading company.
